about.title: Brawley Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Brawley's collisions tend to cluster along a handful of familiar corridors — Main Street, Rt 111, Rt 86, and Old Highway 111 — with public records showing crashes peaking on Wednesday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. In a recent year, Imperial County recorded 38 injury collisions in Brawley, with 49 people hurt and one traffic death. Behind every number is someone dealing with medical bills, missed work, and an insurance adjuster asking questions. LawProactive doesn't handle claims ourselves; we're a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney who works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. If you were injured as a driver, passenger, cyclist, or pedestrian in a Brawley crash, getting matched with someone who can evaluate your situation costs you nothing and starts the process of protecting what you're owed.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity, like a city road crew or public bus, was involved. An attorney can flag deadlines early so a valid claim doesn't get lost to time.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You Fast
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even a partial share of blame can reduce your recovery — insurers know this and often push drivers toward statements that shift blame their way. Speaking with an attorney before giving a recorded statement helps protect your side of the story.

items.title: No Cap Means Every Detail Matters
items.desc: California doesn't cap non-economic damages like pain and suffering, but proving those losses takes documentation — medical records, photos, witness accounts. An attorney can help make sure evidence from the scene and your recovery is preserved before it disappears.

items.question: I was in a crash on Rt 111 near Brawley — how long do I have to take action?
items.answer: In most California car accident cases you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If a government vehicle, road defect, or public entity was involved, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth getting an evaluation sooner rather than later. An independent attorney can look at your specific situation and outline the applicable timeline.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company wants a recorded statement — should I give one?
items.answer: It's generally a good idea to speak with an attorney before agreeing to any recorded statement, since adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim. Anything you say can be reviewed later and taken out of context. Getting free guidance first helps you understand what you're being asked and why.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some responsibility — your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault. This makes it especially important to have someone evaluate the full picture before you accept any fault determination from an insurer. LawProactive can connect you with an attorney who can review the details free of charge.
